meta.title: Failure in removing chinese character in lis-patient-pmi-sync-svc
meta.subject: Removing Chinese characters is skipped after the LIS-10723 data-source upgrade
meta.author: LIS Team

slides.headline: Failure in removing chinese character in lis-patient-pmi-sync-svc
slides.lede: lis-patient-pmi-sync-svc removes Chinese characters when the hospital is on Sybase. After the LIS-10723 data-source upgrade, that flag check does not reach Oracle, so they are not removed.
slides.notes: Patient sync is supposed to remove Chinese characters when the hospital is on Sybase. After the LIS-10723 data-source upgrade, the flag check does not reach Oracle, so they are not removed.

slides.title: Five stops

items.title: Existing Design
items.note: the flag check does not reach Oracle

items.title: Proposed Change
items.note: read the flag, then remove when Sybase

items.title: Promotion and fallback
items.note: new library, or the previous one

items.title: Open Questions
items.note: one Oracle database, and an open transaction

slides.notes: Five stops. Promotion and fallback sit on one slide: ship the library, or put the previous one back.

slides.title: Chinese characters are not removed, so they land in Sybase

steps.title: Non-ASCII characters are removed for Sybase
steps.body: Before a message is stored, patient sync removes Chinese characters when the hospital database is Sybase.

steps.title: data-source gained transaction locking
steps.body: The library upgrade for transaction locking left the Oracle flag check unable to reach Oracle.

steps.title: Characters are not removed
steps.body: Chinese characters are inserted into Sybase.

callout.text: The Oracle flag. When the check fails, the replace is skipped.

slides.notes: The flag is the only thing that decides whether to remove. When the check fails, the program skips the replace and Sybase gets the Chinese characters.

slides.title: The flag check does not reach Oracle

left.label: Today
left.title: Characters are not removed
points: Check: Oracle flag is not read
Result: replace logic does not run
Store: Chinese characters go into Sybase

right.label: Proposed
right.title: Read the flag on Oracle
points: Check: connect to Oracle and read the flag

slides.notes: We do not move the hospital transaction onto Oracle. That would commit hospital work already done. Only the flag read uses the Oracle connection.

slides.title: Read the Oracle flag, then remove when the hospital is Sybase

cards.title: Read the flag on Oracle
cards.body: Connect to Oracle and read the flag while the hospital database is still in use.

cards.title: Sybase means replace
cards.body: If the flag says the hospital is Sybase, replace the Chinese characters.

cards.title: Hospital work stays open
cards.body: Do not switch the hospital transaction over to Oracle.

slides.notes: The replace logic is already in lis-patient-pmi-sync-svc. The library fix is what lets that check succeed.

slides.title: Ship the new library, or put the previous one back

left.title: Promotion
steps: Leave JDBC settings unchanged in DEVQA, SIT, and PROD
Rebuild lis-patient-pmi-sync-svc. Its source stays the same

right.title: Fallback
steps: Redeploy the previous data-source build and restart
On Sybase, the log says defaulting to PostgreSQL
Drop one cached type check for that hospital and lab

slides.notes: DEVQA, SIT, and PROD keep the same JDBC settings. What changes is the library binary. You know the rollback worked when the old warning is back. A wrong saved answer is cleared with DELETE /api/clearCachedDBConn/{hospital}/{lab}.

slides.headline: Q&A
slides.notes: Likely question: does patient sync source change? No. The logic to remove Chinese characters is already there. It runs again once the Oracle flag can be read.
